page.overview:
Who is Ghi?

Ghi headed the military garrison at an Earth Kingdom border town on the Si Wong Desert's edge, where he had to regularly deal with the native Si Wong tribes. To him, there were trustworthy clans who had agreed to serve the Earth Kingdom, and opposing clans who were "rebels and bandits". Ghi was fully aware that a local, decades-long draught was caused by the Earth Kingdom's use of a secretive water pipe network built by the Fire Nation during the Hundred Year War, but deemed the project useful enough in terms of improved regional infrastructure and control to tolerate the locals' suffering from water shortages.

When Kya arrived at Ghi's military base around the 130s AG, having signed up to serve as a healer for isolated settler communities in the desert, Ghi personally greeted her. He warmly thanked her for her service and led her to a local sandbender, Tsetseg, whom he had vetted as being an Earth Kingdom loyalist. Assuring Kya that Tsetseg was a reliable guide, he sent them two on their way to the healer's posting at Liyuan.

A few days later, Kya returned to the base with Tsetseg and Bai Yin Du, the latter being Liyuan's leader. Kya and Tsetseg explained that they had discovered the old Fire Nation pipe network which also led to this base. When Kya claimed that the drought was man-made and could be fixed, Ghi was annoyed and tried to brush off the claim as unfounded.

Kya promptly used her waterbending to rip one of the pipes from the nearby ground, revealing that her statement was true much to Bai Yin's shock. Ghi angrily used his earthbending to carry out an ad hoc repair of the damaged pipe, exclaiming that Kya's act was "vandalism". He explained the network's origin and argued that the Earth Kingdom government was fully aware of its continued operations. As he extolled its allegedly beneficial "streamlining of our irrigation system", Bai Yin asked in horror why the Earth Kingdom loyalists in the area had never been informed of all this. Ghi claimed that there was no need to inform the locals and ordered Bai Yin, Kya and Tsetseg to return to Liyuan, dismissing them as being "deeply unqualified to comment" on the state's infrastructure projects.
